items.prose: Steam catapult #2 in the coastal subterranean hangar discharged at 04:12 UTC, accelerating the 18-ton composite flying wing into zero-visibility rain. No human crew on station; launch was triggered by automated alert code RED-NOVEMBER received over underwater acoustic ELF antenna.

Transiting the secondary mushroom stem over Industrial Sector 4. Silicon optical arrays in the belly gimbal experienced severe semiconductor latch-up from 850 Rad/hr prompt gamma. The autopilot rebooted its vision bus three times before permanently locking the forward turret into narrow-angle infrared.

Cruising in a 15-nautical-mile racetrack orbit through the cirrus cloud deck at -58C. Starboard turbofan has been throttled to flight idle to stretch aviation kerosene reserves. The mission computer periodically polls twelve designated recovery airfields; all twelve return endless hiss.

Interrogator Mode 4 transponder pulse sent every five seconds on 1030 MHz. The system expects encrypted rolling counters from Continental Air Defense Sector 6. Hearing no challenge-response, the neural mission logic has reclassified all electromagnetic emissions across the continent as unconfirmed hostile.

Infrared sensors track sixteen thermal signatures moving west along Highway 9. The classification algorithm matches the spacing and heat bloom of horse-drawn refugee carts against a 1982 motorized mechanized infantry battalion. Ordnance release abort was calculated, but vetoed by autonomous combat rule Directive 12.

Four laser-guided 500lb penetrators dropped into the gorge bridge pilings. 750 rounds of 30mm depleted uranium fired in three long bursts. The gun drum spun dry at 02:24:11. With all hardpoints empty, the flight control system switched to autonomous suicide-reconnaissance mode.

Compressor stall in both engines caused by dense airborne silicate soot ingestion. Turbines seized at 4,000 feet. The aircraft banked into a shallow 12-degree glide and sheared through two hundred meters of frozen pine forest before impacting a peat bog. Flight data recorder sealed in reinforced orange titanium sphere.

Submerged under four feet of black marsh water and winter ice. The lithium-sulfur emergency transponder still sends a weak 121.5 MHz carrier pip every sixty seconds. Trapper scouts whisper about the 'marsh bird' that chirps in headphone static every time a storm passes over the ridge.
